The petitioners in the instant petition have challenged the proceedings in C.C.No.3818/2022 pending before Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.

The petitioners are charged with offences alleged to have been committed under Sections 498A, 323 read with Section 34 of IPC.
2.
The present dispute has arisen due to a matrimonial discord between petitioner no.4-husband and respondent no.2- wife.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the dispute between husband and wife has been settled and they have been granted divorce and the wife has undertaken to cooperate with the husband for quashing of the alleged offences in C.C.No.3818/2022.

He has filed a memo enclosing the memorandum of agreement entered into between the husband and wife,
which has resulted in divorce being granted to them.
NC: 2025:KHC:49538 HC-KAR 3.
Learned counsel for respondent no.2 is absent.

4. Though the parties are not present before the Court, the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent no.1-State also submits that the case may be closed in the light of the settlement arrived at between petitioner no.4 and respondent no.2.
5. It is seen that the petitioners are alleged of committing offences under Sections 498A and 323 read with Section 34 of IPC.
Admittedly, the dispute is a marital in nature.
The parties have arrived at a settlement.
The petitioners are not alleged to have committed any heinous offence.
Quashing of the proceedings against the petitioners will serve the interests of both the complainant (respondent no.2) and the petitioners herein allowing them to lead their life peacefully.

6. Hence, the following:
ORDER i.
The petition is allowed;
NC: 2025:KHC:49538 HC-KAR ii.
The proceedings in C.C.No.3818/2022 pending on the file of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru insofar as it relates to the petitioners herein are concerned stand quashed.

Sd/-
